title: Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Laura Chen
content:
Summary

This policy defines Redwood Inference's standard procedures and controls for contracts, procurement, invoicing and accounts receivable, and revenue recognition. It consolidates approval thresholds, required reviews, procurement lifecycle steps, and specific revenue recognition rules used by Finance and Legal to ensure compliant and consistent accounting and vendor management.

Scope

Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors who engage in purchasing, contracting, or billing activity on behalf of Redwood Inference. Covers: vendor onboarding, purchase orders (POs), contract review and approval, master services agreements (MSAs), statements of work (SOWs), NDAs, invoicing, revenue recognition (ASC 606-aligned), and collections. Excluded: personal reimbursements (see Expense Reimbursement policy).

Roles and Ownership

- Finance (Owner): maintains procurement policies, PO system (ProcureFlow), billing service (fin-billing), revenue recognition templates, and monthly close checklist.
- Legal: contract templates, final legal review and approval for restricted clauses, and custody of executed agreements in DocStore.
- Procurement (shared function): executes vendor onboarding, RFQs, POs for approved spend, and vendor payments.
- Requesting Team (owner-of-need): initiates purchase requests and provides business justification, expected GL coding, and acceptance criteria.
- Sales/Revenue Ops: approves and documents commercial terms impacting revrec (discounts, refunds, custom billing cadence).

Key Systems and Repositories

- DocStore (contract repository) — canonical source of executed agreements.
- ProcureFlow (PO and vendor onboarding) — tracks approvals and POs.
- fin-billing (billing & invoicing service) — generates invoices, posts AR, integrates with accounting ledger.

Policy: Contract Lifecycle and Approvals

1) Intake & Template Selection
   1. Requesting team submits a Contract Request in DocStore with business justification, SOW, and selected template (NDA, MSA, SOW, Professional Services Agreement).
   2. For commonly used templates with no non-standard clauses, Legal fast-track review applies.

2) Review and Redlines
   1. Legal performs clause-level review and marks required redlines. Legal must be looped-in for: data residency clauses, customer data processing (DPA), indemnity > standard, IP assignment, export control, and payment-security terms.
   2. Procurement confirms vendor KYC, insurance certificates, and tax forms before countersignature.

3) Approval Thresholds (approval required before signature)
   - Up to $10,000 (annually or one-time): Requesting Team Manager approval + Procurement intake.
   - $10,001 to $100,000: Finance Manager sign-off + Procurement + Legal (if non-standard terms).
   - $100,001 to $1,000,000: Finance Director + Legal sign-off + VP approval.
   - > $1,000,000 or multiyear commitments > $500,000/year: CFO & General Counsel approval required.

4) Turnaround SLOs (targets)
   - NDAs (standard): 3 business days.
   - Standard MSA (template, no non-standard terms): 7 business days.
   - SOWs & PSAs: 7-14 business days depending on complexity.
   - Complex agreements (data residency, extensive indemnities): 15+ business days.

5) Execution and Storage
   - All signed agreements must be uploaded to DocStore within 24 hours of signature. ProcureFlow entry must be completed before the first vendor invoice is paid.

Legal Review Checklist (required items to confirm)

- Parties and legal names verified.
- Effective date and term clearly stated.
- Payment terms defined (currency, method, invoicing cadence).
- Termination and renewal provisions reviewed.
- Confidentiality, data protection, and DPA triggers assessed.
- IP and deliverables ownership clauses confirmed.
- Limitation of liability and indemnification reviewed and approved.
- Insurance and compliance obligations present and verified.

Procurement Procedure (standard purchase flow)

1) Request: Requesting team opens a ProcureFlow request with cost center, GL code, vendor name, business justification, and supporting SOW/quote.
2) Sourcing: Procurement completes RFQ (if > $50k preferred) or confirms single-source justification.
3) Approval: ProcureFlow routes for required approvals per thresholds above.
4) PO Issuance: On approval, Procurement issues PO from ProcureFlow; PO number must appear on vendor invoices.
5) Receiving & Acceptance: Requesting team confirms delivery of goods/services, attaches acceptance evidence to ProcureFlow.
6) Invoice Processing: AP matches invoice to PO and acceptance record; exceptions routed to Requesting Team and Procurement.

Procurement Controls and Required Documentation

- Vendor onboarding packet: W-9 (US) / tax form, certificate of insurance, bank details (or payment portal), primary contract, anti-corruption screening confirmation.
- Single-source justification required for purchases > $50k.
- Capital vs Expense determination must be noted on the request (Finance provides guidance).

Payment Terms, Billing and Collections

- Standard payment terms: Net 30 from invoice date for vendor invoices, unless a vendor contract specifies otherwise and is approved by Finance.
- Customer billing cadence: hosted subscriptions billed monthly in arrears by default; dedicated and enterprise contracts may be billed monthly or quarterly in advance per commercial terms.
- Discounts, credits, refunds: require Sales/Revenue Ops documentation and Finance approval before issuance.
- Collections / dunning schedule for customer AR: 7 days past due - reminder; 30 days - escalation to Sales/Account Owner; 60 days - collections team outreach and hold on account features; 90+ days - legal review for potential write-off or litigation.

Revenue Recognition (principles and common scenarios)

Redwood follows ASC 606 principles. Core rules and examples: 

- Identify the contract: An agreement with enforceable rights and obligations (signed MSA/SOW, or written order).
- Identify performance obligations: distinct promises (e.g., subscription access, professional services deliverables).
- Determine transaction price: consideration expected, adjusted for discounts, variable consideration, and incentives.
- Allocate price to performance obligations: using standalone selling price (SSP) or best estimate.
- Recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.

Common recognition treatments:

- Subscription fees (hosted API): recognized ratably over the service period (monthly SaaS recognized daily pro rata across the month). If billed in advance, record deferred revenue and recognize ratably.
- Dedicated capacity reservation fees (committed capacity): if the fee grants a right to service over a period, recognize ratably over the commitment term.
- Professional services (implementation, customization): recognize over time if criteria for over-time recognition are met (customer controls work-in-progress or enforceable right to payment for work performed). Otherwise recognize at completion (percentage-of-completion or milestone-based with documented acceptance criteria).
- One-time setup fees: generally deferred and recognized over the expected benefit period (commonly aligned with subscription term) unless a separate performance obligation exists.
- Variable consideration (e.g., usage discounts, credits): estimate using expected value or most likely amount; constrain estimates when necessary to avoid significant reversal.
- Contract modifications: treat as separate contract or as modification depending on scope and price changes per ASC 606 guidelines.

Documentation & Month-End Close Requirements

- All new contracts must include RevRec mapping fields in DocStore: contract start/end dates, performance obligations, transaction price, billing cadence, and accounting team revenue owner.
- Finance posts monthly journal entries for deferred revenue and recognizes revenue per schedules reconciled to fin-billing.
- For contracts with variable consideration or complex terms, Finance will prepare a revrec memo and attach to the month close pack.

Invoicing examples

- Example invoice metadata (required fields): PO number, MSA/SOW reference, invoice date, invoice number, line-level description, quantity, unit price, taxes, payment instructions.

- Sample invoice JSON (for fin-billing ingestion):

  {
    "invoice_number": "INV-2026-1234",
    "po_number": "PO-7890",
    "contract_ref": "MSA-2026-567",
    "invoice_date": "2026-10-01",
    "lines": ["Hosted API subscription \u2014 October 2026"],
    "amount_due": "15000.00"
  }

Retention and Recordkeeping

- Contracts and invoices: retain for a minimum of 7 years (legal or tax may require longer retention in specific jurisdictions).
- ProcureFlow and DocStore are the authoritative sources for POs and contracts. Backups must be maintained per IT retention policy.

Exceptions, Escalations and Policy Deviations

- Deviations from this policy require a documented exception request submitted to Finance with clear business justification and approval by the appropriate approver (minimum Finance Director for monetary exceptions).
- Escalation path: Requesting Team -> Procurement -> Finance Manager -> Finance Director -> CFO/General Counsel (if required).

Change History

- 2025-03-10: Initial policy created.
- 2026-06-15: Updated approval thresholds and added ProcureFlow requirement for PO on first invoice.
- 2026-11-20: Clarified revrec treatment for committed capacity and standardised turnaround SLOs.
